I am a quantitative social science researcher studying how scientists and other highly skilled workers move across organisations and cities, how relational ties shape mobility decisions, and how mobility reorganises collaboration and knowledge production.

## Research Themes

::: {.theme-grid}
::: {.theme-card}
<span>01</span>
<h3>Scientific Careers & Mobility</h3>

How do scientists choose destinations and move between organisations, cities, and countries?
:::

::: {.theme-card}
<span>02</span>
<h3>Collaboration Networks & Relational Capital</h3>

How do pre-existing collaboration ties affect mobility, and which relationships remain valuable across organisational boundaries?
:::

::: {.theme-card}
<span>03</span>
<h3>Innovation & Knowledge Production</h3>

How does researcher mobility reshape collaboration, knowledge diffusion, and regional innovation?
:::
:::

:::

::: {.page-band}

## Evidence Base

::: {.profile-grid .profile-grid-three}
::: {.profile-item}
### Longitudinal Career Data

Verified work reconstructs career, institution, city, publication, collaboration, and mobility records for elite biomedical scientists from 1970 to 2023.
:::

::: {.profile-item}
### Relational and Spatial Methods

Current manuscripts use social network analysis, mobility ego networks, WERGM, event-specific candidate sets, and conditional logit models.
:::

::: {.profile-item}
### Research Outputs

The public record includes an accepted first-author article, submitted manuscripts, a master's thesis, selected research outputs, and a public Scopus linkage toolkit.
:::
:::
